title: Proper direct image, base change and projection formula for $\mathcal O_E$
statement:
Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite and $p\colon X\to Y$ proper between standing schemes.

1. For $K\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$, $Rp_*K$ is derived $\pi_E$-complete, and
   $(Rp_*K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}\cO_{E,Y}/\pi_E\simeq Rp_*(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\cO_{E,X}/\pi_E)$;
   hence $Rp_*K\in\Dbc(Y,\cO_E)$.
2. (Derived Nakayama.) A derived $\pi_E$-complete $C$ with $C\otimes^{\mathbf L}\cO_E/\pi_E=0$ is
   zero.
3. The proper base change map and the projection formula map are isomorphisms for
   $K\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$, $M\in\Dbc(Y,\cO_E)$.

proof.text: Put $A=\cO_E$, $\pi=\pi_E$, $P_n=A/\pi^n$, $\kappa=P_1$. The DVR and quotient lemmas give Noetherian $A$ and finite perfect $P_n$; $\ell\in(\pi)$ since $|\ell|_E<1$, so $\ell\kappa=0$. The integral-limit and cartesian-coefficient statements identify the pulled-back rings with the completed rings and their exact pullbacks. These verify the adic datum for the direct-image theorem. The operations are the derived module functors of module-derived-pushpull.

source.place: (1): coefficient hypotheses; Stacks 099N (lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case) and the existing completed-coefficient comparison.

proof.text: For an integral constructible $L$, integral-models (2) gives completeness and classical bounded constructible $L_1$. Its constant-coefficient formulation gives finite Tor dimension; constant-coefficient comparison (3) identifies this with $L_1\in\Dctf(T,\kappa)$. The reductions criterion gives the uniform bounded finite-level domain required by operation-reduction.

source.place: (1): integral-models criterion and the domains of finite reduction.

proof.text: Apply direct-image-limits: $Rp_*K$ is complete and its canonical finite-reduction comparisons are isomorphisms. For $n=1$, operation-reduction identifies this with $Rp_*K_1$ in $D(\kappa_Y)$, retaining the scalar action. The finite proper theorem (1) makes this bounded constructible; constructible comparison makes it classical. Integral-models (2) therefore gives $Rp_*K\in\Dbc(Y,A)$, proving (1).

source.place: (1): completeness, canonical reduction and constructible finiteness; Stacks 099M, 099N and 09AI (lemmas compare-constructible and compare-constructible-derived).

proof.text: For complete $C$ with $C_1=0$, apply the first-reduction Nakayama statement to obtain $C=0$, proving (2); it requires no boundedness.

source.place: (2): derived Nakayama, supplied by the existing first-reduction node.

proof.text: In the standing cartesian square, permanence makes $p\prime$ proper and $X\prime$ standing: finite type and separatedness compose with $Y\prime\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Integral-models (3), followed by step 3 for $p,p\prime$, puts both endpoints of exchange and of projection in $\Dbc$, hence makes them complete by integral-models (2).

source.place: (3): completeness of the four endpoints; standing setting retained.

proof.text: Exchange is the unit--pullback-comparison--counit composite. Operation-reduction identifies its endpoints in the finite-coefficient categories and preserves these units and counits; the pullback comparison is the same tensor reassociation after reduction. Thus the reduced composite is exactly $\beta_{K_1}$. Projection is the adjunct of $(\varepsilon_K\otimes1)t_p$. The same tensor, unit and counit compatibilities make its reduction exactly $\alpha_{K_1,M_1}$.

source.place: (3): reduction of the specified canonical maps; Stacks 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map) specifies the projection adjunct.

proof.text: By step 2, $K_1,M_1$ have finite Tor dimension; $\kappa$ is finite and killed by $\ell$. The finite proper theorem (2),(3) makes both reduced maps isomorphisms. Their integral endpoints are complete by step 5, so the first-reduction isomorphism criterion makes both integral maps isomorphisms, proving (3).

source.place: (3): finite-coefficient isomorphisms and the existing complete-cone/Nakayama criterion.

proof_origin.place: Paragraphs (1)--(3), expanded using existing DAG statements; Stacks Tags 099N, 099M, 099L, 09AI and 0B56 checked in the local sources. The proof keeps the unit route through finite coefficients and integral models.

tool_uses.why: Identifies the first-reduction constructibility criterion with the uniform finite-level bounded category in which the generic operation-reduction lemma is stated.
General completed-coefficient direct-image/derived-limit and finite-perfect-reduction comparison, used to implement the unit's 099L argument, not to replace its finite-coefficient finiteness route.

Only its ordinary pullback/tensor/direct-image coefficient comparisons and preservation of the units and counits forming exchange/projection are used; it asserts no proper base change or projection isomorphism. The current unit does not contain this generic compatibility lemma.

Step 4 cites its vanishing assertion (complete K with K_1=0 is zero) for clause (2), as the blueprint proof of (2) itself cites the derived-Nakayama unit; step 7 cites its isomorphism criterion for morphisms of derived complete complexes, which replaces the unit's final cone argument (closure under cones plus vanishing).
Its reduction comparison transports the finite Tor condition in the constant-coefficient definition of Dc to the actual completed-coefficient first reduction.
Identifies the pulled-back integral coefficient sheaf with the completed sheaf used by the direct-image tool; this prevents conflating it with constant coefficients.
Classicality of the bounded constructible finite-coefficient output, needed by the integral criterion, is the standard comparison input already specified by the unit.
Ensures exact inverse image on the coefficient sheaves and identifies the ringed-topos functors and squares used in the generic reduction tools.
Checks Noetherianity of the coefficient ring and the finite residue field for the generic adic datum.
Supplies finite-set and perfectness hypotheses for the coefficient quotients in the generic direct-image theorem.

Its proof derives the transposes for exchange and projection squares, so a new node would only restate it. (6) the ambient exchange (eta; theta; epsilon) and the projection adjunct reduce exactly to the finite maps. (7) finite (2),(3) and the isomorphism criterion prove clause (3). The dropped proof_deps (dc-setting, derived-completion, nakayama-resolution) are no longer used, and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses.
